   DOOR KNOBS
      Door knobs are relatively easy to throw and are great for individualising your
     home. By adjusting the size you throw them to, the knobs can be adapted to ﬁt
     any surface – doors, kitchen cupboards, chests of drawers, etc, and colour co-
                       ordinated perfectly to match your décor





   You will need:                       ■ Tools for throwing – water bowl, sponge, cutting                                                                     wire, ribs
   ■ Clay – stoneware preferably, for durability
                                       ■ Glaze of choice to suit clay type

   Before you begin:
     These knobs are all thrown individually on batts, but an alternative approach would be to throw them oﬀ the
    hump.
       Prepare your clay by kneading it well to remove any possible trapped air, then ﬁx a batt to the wheel head –
    you can ﬁ nd full instructions on how to throw a pad for a batt in issue 65 if you don’t have a quick-ﬁx mechanism
      for your wheel.
      To make knobs for use on doors, you will need 100-200g of clay for each. For cupboard knobs, the weight
    would need to be halved, making them much more diﬃ cult to throw individually and therefore more suitable for
     throwing oﬀ the hump.
       Note: there is great scope for experimentation when throwing knobs, and deciding on a shape is really down
     to individual taste and requirements, but it is worth practising to see how many you can create. Just bear in mind
     that a knob should be comfortable and pleasant to handle.
